title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to have her urologist appointment transcribed by artificial intelligence, but the AI scribe invented a claim that she used psychedelic mushrooms. She found the false statement in a letter sent to her GP after kidney stone surgery and worried it could harm her workers' compensation case. The urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates about 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes.

A Digital Rights Watch report found other serious errors, including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and inventing epilepsy. The Therapeutic Goods Administration has been reviewing AI scribes and says its findings will be released in the coming weeks, with any breaches acted upon. The advocacy group wants the AI Safety Institute to test scribes and publish approved tools. Ms Green said she would only consent to AI transcription again if she had an established relationship with a doctor.
